title: Release process
text: main carries clean released version — .9000. (Earlier releases put .9000 main; dropped 1.1.0. README/badge tweak main version number normal fine — need version marker.) Routing: Routine work (R code, man/, vignettes, tests, docs) — branch dev, PR dev. reaches main via release. Urgent patch / hotfix released line — branch main, fix, set DESCRIPTION next patch (X.Y.(Z+1)), PR main, release , merge main -> dev fix flows dev line. (“bug fixes go main” path: ship patch without dragging dev’s unfinished features.) Cosmetic / GitHub-facing fixes (README prose, badges, figures, pkgdown config) — branch main, PR main. version change; main stays released number. Release ops (tag, GitHub Release) — directly main (documented exception branch+PR rule). Keep sync: main-side fix, merge main -> dev flows dev line. Skipping produces “fix, two parallel PRs” situation.

title: Package Architecture
text: TemporalHazard pure-R reimplementation C/SAS HAZARD procedure originally developed University Alabama Birmingham (UAB) multi-phase parametric hazard modeling (Blackstone, Naftel, Turner 1986). SAS/C code R package currently developed maintained Cleveland Clinic Foundation, R code wholly developed Cleveland Clinic Foundation. package provides unified framework fitting additive hazard models arbitrary number temporal phases, governed three-parameter decompos(t; t_half, nu, m) family. generalized temporal decomposition extends naturally longitudinal mixed-effects settings (Rajeswaran et al. 2018). vignette documents internal architecture: source files organized, functions compose fitting pipeline, golden fixtures ensure regression-free development, reference datasets ship package.

title: Package Architecture
text: primary user entry point hazard(), dispatches distribution-specific optimizers. diagram shows call flow multiphase fit. single-phase distributions (Weibull, exponential, log-logistic, log-normal), hazard() dispatches corresponding .hzr_optim_<dist>() function, calls .hzr_optim_generic() distribution-specific log-likelihood gradient. multiphase model concatenates per-phase sub-vectors single flat theta internal (estimation) scale: Internal theta layout per phase .hzr_split_theta() partitions concatenated vector named list per-phase sub-vectors. .hzr_unpack_phase_theta() extracts named parameters (log_mu, log_t_half, nu, m, beta) sub-vector. hzr_phase(type, t_half, nu, m, formula) creates lightweight S3 object stores phase type, initial shape parameters, optional phase-specific covariate formula. constructor validates inputs returns NA shape parameters constant phases. list hzr_phase objects validated .hzr_validate_phases(), auto-names unnamed phases (“phase_1”, “phase_2”, …) catches common mistake passing bare hzr_phase instead list. hzr_decompos(time, t_half, nu, m) mathematical core. computes G(t) (CDF), g(t) (density), h(t) (hazard) three-parameter family across six valid sign combinations nu m. phase-level helpers hzr_phase_cumhaz() hzr_phase_hazard() wrap hzr_decompos() apply phase type mapping: .hzr_optim_multiphase() runs multi-start strategy: first start uses assembled starting values (theta hzr_phase specs); subsequent starts perturb randomly (sd = 0.5). best log-likelihood across starts kept. helps optimizer escape shallow local optima common multiphase models. optimizer delegates .hzr_optim_generic(), wraps stats::optim() method "BFGS" (unconstrained; scale parameters log-transformed). Hessian computed numerically converged point variance-covariance estimation.

Decomposition consistency —Verifies phase additivity CDF saturation C reference parameter values. Conservation events —Checks model-implied expected events (\(\sum [1 - \exp(-H(t_i))]\)) matches observed event count (545), reported C binary (544.9993). title: Package Architecture
text: TemporalHazard ships five clinical reference datasets inst/extdata/, converted original C/SAS HAZARD test data. datasets used vignette examples parity testing. Reference datasets (lazy-loaded via data()) AVC dataset contains 310 patients underwent repair atrioventricular septal defects. primary example dataset used throughout hazard modeling examples richest set covariates multivariable analysis. AVC dataset variables KUL dataset large series 5880 primary isolated CABG patients KU Leuven (1971–July 1987). serves primary benchmark C binary parity testing simplest structure (intercept-, right-censored) combined large sample size exercises three temporal phases. original SAS analysis (hz.deadp.KUL.sas) also includes return--angina reintervention endpoints (recorded original fixed-width file 6 columns), death endpoint (int_dead, dead) extracted parity testing. OMC dataset contains 339 patients unique collection involves repeated thromboembolic events (3 per patient) left censoring. SAS analysis transforms dataset repeated-events format using STARTTME CENSORED indicators, exercising interval censoring likelihood. TGA dataset contains 470 patients underwent arterial switch operation. includes derived variables (logarithmic inverse transforms clinical measurements) primarily used sensitivity analysis internal validation examples. VALVES dataset largest multivariable example 1533 patients multiple endpoints (death, prosthetic valve endocarditis, bioprosthesis degeneration, reoperation). SAS analysis (hm.deadp.VALVES.sas) fits multivariable 3-phase model 10 covariates across multiple event types.

title: Package Architecture
text: original C/SAS HAZARD procedure uses different parameterization TemporalHazard. hzr_argument_mapping() function documents full translation. SAS HAZARD R parameter mapping (excerpt) SAS early phase uses four parameters: DELTA, RHO (THALF), NU, M. collapse onto three-parameter decompos family: DELTA —Time transformation B(t) = (exp(delta*t) - 1)/delta. DELTA = 0 (common case), B(t) = t transformation absorbed. Non-zero DELTA currently supported. RHO / THALF —Scale parameter. RHO = NU * THALF * ((2^M - 1)/M)^NU. Maps directly t_half hzr_phase(). NU —Time exponent. Maps directly. M —Shape exponent. Maps directly. SAS late phase uses G3 decomposition four parameters, now directly supported via hzr_phase("g3", ...): TAU –> tau (scale parameter) GAMMA –> gamma (time exponent) ALPHA –> alpha (shape parameter; alpha = 0 gives exponential case) ETA –> eta (outer exponent) G3 formula (alpha > 0) : \(G_3(t) = \left(\left((t/\tau)^\gamma + 1\right)^{1/\alpha} - 1\right)^\eta\) Unlike G1, G3 unbounded —can grow without limit, making suitable late-phase rising hazards. KUL benchmark gamma = 3, alpha = 1, eta = 1, simplifies \(G_3(t) = t^3\).

title: Fitting Hazard Models
text: Right censoring far common censoring type clinical survival data — patient still alive last follow-, know event time exceeds observed window. Two types arise frequently enough warrant explicit handling. Interval censoring occurs event known happened two observation times, specific time. canonical example clinic-visit data: patient confirmed alive month 12 found dead month 24, event occurred somewhere \((12, 24)\). naive analysis treats event right-censored 12 exactly observed 24; introduce bias. Left censoring mirror: event occurred first observation time (time_upper), already established moment first contact — \(T \leq t_{\text{upper}}\). package encodes censoring type status vector: interval-censored rows, supply time_lower time_upper directly hazard(). formula interface handles Surv(time, status) right-censored data Surv(start, stop, event) counting-process (repeating-event) data; interval censoring passed via direct arguments. simulate 400 cardiac surgery patients observed semi-annual clinic visits (every 6 months, 4–8 scheduled visits per patient). event falls two consecutive visits observation interval-censored; falls last visit patient right-censored. Note time_lower counting-process entry time. Weibull multiphase likelihoods, time_lower doubles entry (left-truncation) time right-censored exact-event rows (status %% c(0, 1)): 0 < time_lower < time, row contributes H(stop) − H(start), counting-process form used epoch-decomposed repeated events. ordinary right-censored event row entry time, leave time_lower 0 omit . Setting time_lower = time treated entry — time_lower acts entry time strictly less time, longer zeroes row’s contribution. exponential, log-logistic, log-normal likelihoods use time_lower entry time unaffected. Fit Weibull model using censoring types: naive analyst doesn’t visit-bracket data record death discovery visit (time_upper) rather interval. overstates event time — patient appears survived longer — biasing estimated hazard shape. interval-censored fit recovers parameters accurately. naive fit estimates \(\mu\) comparably introduces substantial positive bias \(\nu\) — sees events consistently appearing visit times (every 6 months) infers sharper, periodic hazard shape doesn’t match underlying exponential structure.
code: set.seed(101) n         <- 400 visit_gap <- 6   # months between visits  # True event times: Weibull mu = 0.025, nu = 1.0 (median ~28 months) true_time <- rexp(n, rate = 0.025)  # nu=1 → exponential  n_visits  <- sample(4:8, n, replace = TRUE)  status     <- integer(n) time       <- numeric(n) time_lower <- numeric(n) time_upper <- numeric(n)  for (i in seq_len(n)) {   visits <- seq(visit_gap, n_visits[i] * visit_gap, by = visit_gap)   t_ev   <- true_time[i]   brk    <- findInterval(t_ev, c(0, visits))  # which interval contains t_ev    if (brk > length(visits)) {     # Event after last visit: right-censored.     # time_lower = 0: with H(time_lower) = H(0) = 0, the right-censored     # contribution reduces to -(H(time) - H(0)) = -H(time), which is correct.     status[i]     <- 0L     time[i]       <- max(visits)     time_lower[i] <- 0     time_upper[i] <- max(visits)   } else {     # Event within the visit window: interval-censored in (lower, upper)     lower_bound   <- if (brk == 1L) 0 else visits[brk - 1L]     upper_bound   <- visits[brk]     status[i]     <- 2L     time[i]       <- lower_bound     time_lower[i] <- lower_bound     time_upper[i] <- upper_bound   } }  table(status) #> status #>   0   2  #> 168 232 fit_ic <- hazard(   time       = time,   status     = status,   time_lower = time_lower,   time_upper = time_upper,   dist  = "weibull",   theta = c(mu = 0.025, nu = 1.0),   fit   = TRUE )  fit_ic #> hazard object #>   observations: 400  #>   predictors:   0  #>   dist:         weibull  #>   engine:       native-r-m2  #>   log-lik:      -674.374  #>   converged:    TRUE # Naive: treat each interval-censored row as an exact event at time_upper # (the visit when the death was first recorded) fit_naive <- hazard(   time   = ifelse(status == 2L, time_upper, time),   status = ifelse(status == 2L, 1L,         status),   dist  = "weibull",   theta = c(mu = 0.025, nu = 1.0),   fit   = TRUE )  # Compare MLEs; true parameters are mu = 0.025, nu = 1.0 rbind(   interval_censored = round(coef(fit_ic)[1:2],   4),   naive_exact_upper = round(coef(fit_naive)[1:2], 4),   truth             = c(mu = 0.025, nu = 1.0) ) #>                       mu     nu #> interval_censored 0.0251 1.0345 #> naive_exact_upper 0.0259 1.4566 #> truth             0.0250 1.0000

code: # Naive: treat each interval-censored row as an exact event at time_upper # (the visit when the death was first recorded) fit_naive <- hazard(   time   = ifelse(status == 2L, time_upper, time),   status = ifelse(status == 2L, 1L,         status),   dist  = "weibull",   theta = c(mu = 0.025, nu = 1.0),   fit   = TRUE )  # Compare MLEs; true parameters are mu = 0.025, nu = 1.0 rbind(   interval_censored = round(coef(fit_ic)[1:2],   4),   naive_exact_upper = round(coef(fit_naive)[1:2], 4),   truth             = c(mu = 0.025, nu = 1.0) ) #>                       mu     nu #> interval_censored 0.0251 1.0345 #> naive_exact_upper 0.0259 1.4566 #> truth             0.0250 1.0000

title: Fitting Hazard Models
text: ’ve now seen phase type use: "cdf" early phase AVC operative mortality, "constant" phase AVC background rate, implicit single shape every Weibull fit. package supports three phase types total, summarized quick reference: "cdf" type covers widest range shapes: setting t_half small (e.g., 0.5) creates early-peaking phase; setting large (e.g., 10) creates late-rising phase. "constant" phase needs shape parameters. "g3" shape explicit late-rising parameterization matches SAS HAZARD “late” library; use need parity C/SAS reference fit, late rise clear lag--accelerate pattern delayed "cdf" doesn’t capture cleanly. See vignette("mf-mathematical-foundations") full mathematical treatment , including parameter identifiability constraints.

title: Getting Started with TemporalHazard
text: simulated data 180 patients three plausible risk covariates — age, NYHA functional class, cardiogenic shock. fit single Weibull hazard: scale parameter (mu) shape exponent (nu) lets hazard accelerate nu > 1, decelerate nu < 1, stay flat nu = 1. Weibull natural starting point single-distribution fit covers three monotone shapes just two parameters. hazard() interface takes survival formula (Surv(time, status) left, covariates right), starting-value vector (theta), distribution name. Passing fit = TRUE runs optimizer returns fitted model; passing fit = FALSE returns model specification without fitting, useful sanity-checking formula starting values committing optimizer.
code: library(TemporalHazard) library(survival)  set.seed(1001) n <- 180 dat <- data.frame(   time = rexp(n, rate = 0.35) + 0.05,   status = rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = 0.6),   age = rnorm(n, mean = 62, sd = 11),   nyha = sample(1:4, n, replace = TRUE),   shock = rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = 0.18) )  fit <- TemporalHazard::hazard(   Surv(time, status) ~ age + nyha + shock,   data = dat,   theta = c(mu = 0.25, nu = 1.10, beta1 = 0, beta2 = 0, beta3 = 0),   dist = "weibull",   fit = TRUE,   control = list(maxit = 300) )  summary(fit) #> hazard model summary #>   observations: 180  #>   predictors:   3  #>   dist:         weibull  #>   engine:       native-r-m2  #>   converged:    TRUE  #>   log-lik:      -293.553  #>   evaluations: fn=36, gr=8 #>  #> Coefficients: #>          estimate   std_error      z_stat      p_value #> mu    0.121860518 0.062260593  1.95726560 5.031625e-02 #> nu    1.143730632 0.084302528 13.56697905 6.285984e-42 #> beta1 0.001716551 0.008807986  0.19488579 8.454824e-01 #> beta2 0.156208724 0.090597558  1.72420458 8.467092e-02 #> beta3 0.017352702 0.362918430  0.04781433 9.618642e-01

title: Getting Started with TemporalHazard
text: fitted hazard model lets score new patients without refitting. predict() method takes newdata frame type argument selects quantity compute: "linear_predictor" — covariate-driven log-hazard-ratio row, \(x^\top \beta\). "hazard" — hazard multiplier, \(\exp(x^\top \beta)\). "survival" — probability surviving past row’s time, \(S(t \mid x)\). "cumulative_hazard" — integrated hazard row’s time, \(H(t \mid x) = -\log S(t \mid x)\). three rows made-patients spanning covariate range training data: younger, low-NYHA, -shock patient early time; middle case median; older, high-NYHA, shock patient . compute four prediction types .
code: new_patients <- data.frame(   time = c(0.5, 1.5, 3.0),   age = c(50, 65, 75),   nyha = c(1, 3, 4),   shock = c(0, 0, 1) )  pred_input <- new_patients  new_patients$linear_predictor <- predict(fit, newdata = pred_input, type = "linear_predictor") new_patients$hazard_multiplier <- predict(fit, newdata = pred_input, type = "hazard") new_patients$survival <- predict(fit, newdata = pred_input, type = "survival") new_patients$cumulative_hazard <- predict(fit, newdata = pred_input, type = "cumulative_hazard")  new_patients #>   time age nyha shock linear_predictor hazard_multiplier  survival #> 1  0.5  50    1     0        0.2420363          1.273840 0.9494097 #> 2  1.5  65    3     0        0.5802020          1.786399 0.7743185 #> 3  3.0  75    4     1        0.7709289          2.161774 0.5046535 #>   cumulative_hazard #> 1        0.05191482 #> 2        0.25577202 #> 3        0.68388317

title: Getting Started with TemporalHazard
text: Weibull fit describes hazard one smooth, monotone curve — can rise, fall, stay flat time, change direction. ’s fine processes (light bulbs failing, parts wearing ). breaks quickly clinical data. Consider CABG (coronary artery bypass graft) surgery. days right operation risk death highest: patient ICU, exposed operative complications, infections, bleeding. survive window risk drops low, roughly flat background rate: recover, go home, live lives. Years later risk rises grafts begin deteriorate cohort ages. Three distinct regimes, clinical mechanism. single Weibull (log-normal, monotone distribution) can fit three . optimizer compromise: picking shape ’s mediocre everywhere instead right one regime. ’d predict early deaths, wrong slope middle, late deaths. multiphase decomposition workaround. Instead asking one distribution everything, describe total cumulative hazard sum phase-specific contributions, temporal shape: \[H(t \mid x) = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \mu_j(x) \cdot \Phi_j(t)\] \(\Phi_j(t)\) phase-specific temporal shape: unit-scaled curve says phase \(j\)’s hazard accumulates time. \(\mu_j(x)\) phase-specific scale: much cumulative hazard belongs phase \(j\), possibly modulated covariates. phases overlap hazards add. ’s switching, thresholds, piecewise joins; time \(t\) instantaneous hazard \(h(t) = dH/dt\) sum per-phase contributions \(\mu_j \cdot \phi_j(t)\), \(\phi_j = d\Phi_j/dt\). number phases modeling lever lets match data’s actual structure. processes well-described two phases (early failure + steady-state). cardiac-surgery cohorts need three: early operative risk + constant background + late deterioration. small handful — acute aortic dissection classic — need four (operative + subacute + constant + late). framework general; count modeling choice driven clinical knowledge shape Kaplan-Meier cumulative hazard curve. CABGKUL fit use three phases. ’s property package; ’s property dataset. phase specified hzr_phase(). first argument picks shape function: "cdf" saturating curve bounded 0 1 (SAS “early” / G1 shape), "constant" flat hazard plateau (SAS “G2”), "g3" polynomial late-rising shape SAS “late” library. Remaining arguments set shape’s free parameters, fix fixed = "shapes". Phase types section full menu. fit use textbook three-phase decomposition: saturating early peak, constant background, polynomial late rise. fix shapes can compare fitted scales published reference; work usually estimate . summary marks rows NA std_error, z_stat, p_value columns. Two mechanisms produce , deliberate: seven shape parameters carry fixed = "shapes" act user-supplied constants (t_half, nu, m early phase; tau, gamma, alpha, eta late phase). optimizer never moves , estimated variance report. One three log_mu scale parameters also NA. default multiphase optimizer enforces Conservation Events (Turner’s theorem): one phase’s log_mu solved analytically every iteration total predicted events equal total observed. phase free parameter MLE, inverse-Hessian variance degenerate, table marks NA rather print misleading number. Pass control = list(conserve = FALSE) disable Conservation Events estimate three scale parameters freely. two remaining log_mu rows optimizer-estimated free parameters; Wald statistics reflect two-parameter fit dimension remains Conservation--Events constraint absorbs third log_mu. MLE numbers summary tell us model committed , three phases fit together time. need per-phase contributions. decompose = TRUE argument predict() returns one cumulative-hazard column per phase plus total; numerically differentiate one (coarse first-difference fine , since just want look) get instantaneous hazard rate. plot follows diagnostic matters: shows whether model carved timeline way expected. early phase dominate near \(t = 0\) die . constant phase flat floor. late phase near zero early rise lag. shapes looks wrong, fix starting values choice shape function, data. Figure 2: Additive phase decomposition: total hazard (solid) = early + constant + late (dashed) decomposition plot tells us model right shape; overlay plot tells us right level. Plotting parametric survival curve Kaplan-Meier estimate axis single useful diagnostic hazard fit. KM gold-standard nonparametric reference; parametric curve drifts away , something wrong model iterations won’t fix. Figure 3: Multiphase parametric survival vs. Kaplan-Meier Picking right phase shape single biggest modeling decision multiphase fit. package ships canonical shapes SAS C HAZARD library: "cdf" — saturating curve \(\Phi(t) \[0, 1]\), parameterized t_half (time \(G(t_{1/2}) = 0.5\)), nu (time exponent), m (shape exponent). SAS “early” G1 shape. Use early phase, phase whose accumulated hazard saturates rather growing without bound. "constant" — \(\Phi(t) = t\). phase’s hazard rate flat; shape parameters estimate, scale \(\mu\). SAS G2 shape. Use background plateau. "g3" — SAS “late” shape, parameterized tau (time-scale), gamma (time exponent), alpha (shape parameter; \(\alpha = 0\) gives exponential limit), eta (outer exponent). Use late phase near-zero early accelerates time — graft deterioration years archetype. See ?hzr_phase additional "hazard" shape full parameterization . practice choose phase shapes looking Kaplan-Meier cumulative hazard plot, identifying regimes present, matching regime shape family whose behavior fits. fit, look decomposition plot, adjust starting values fix shapes phase doesn’t land expected. "g3" type uses four-parameter G3 decomposition original C/SAS HAZARD program, providing unbounded power-law growth late-phase hazards. See vignette("mf-mathematical-foundations") full mathematical treatment.

list(     early    = hzr_phase("cdf", t_half = 0.2, nu = 1, m = 1,                           fixed = "shapes"),     constant = hzr_phase("constant"),     late     = hzr_phase("g3",  tau = 1, gamma = 3, alpha = 1, eta = 1,                           fixed = "shapes")   ),   fit     = TRUE,   control = list(n_starts = 5, maxit = 1000) )  summary(fit_mp) #> Multiphase hazard model (3 phases) #> title: Getting Started with TemporalHazard
text: number phases modeling lever lets match data’s actual structure. processes well-described two phases (early failure + steady-state). cardiac-surgery cohorts need three: early operative risk + constant background + late deterioration. small handful — acute aortic dissection classic — need four (operative + subacute + constant + late). framework general; count modeling choice driven clinical knowledge shape Kaplan-Meier cumulative hazard curve. CABGKUL fit use three phases. ’s property package; ’s property dataset. phase specified hzr_phase(). first argument picks shape function: "cdf" saturating curve bounded 0 1 (SAS “early” / G1 shape), "constant" flat hazard plateau (SAS “G2”), "g3" polynomial late-rising shape SAS “late” library. Remaining arguments set shape’s free parameters, fix fixed = "shapes". Phase types section full menu. fit use textbook three-phase decomposition: saturating early peak, constant background, polynomial late rise. fix shapes can compare fitted scales published reference; work usually estimate . summary marks rows NA std_error, z_stat, p_value columns. Two mechanisms produce , deliberate: seven shape parameters carry fixed = "shapes" act user-supplied constants (t_half, nu, m early phase; tau, gamma, alpha, eta late phase). optimizer never moves , estimated variance report. One three log_mu scale parameters also NA. default multiphase optimizer enforces Conservation Events (Turner’s theorem): one phase’s log_mu solved analytically every iteration total predicted events equal total observed. phase free parameter MLE, inverse-Hessian variance degenerate, table marks NA rather print misleading number. Pass control = list(conserve = FALSE) disable Conservation Events estimate three scale parameters freely. two remaining log_mu rows optimizer-estimated free parameters; Wald statistics reflect two-parameter fit dimension remains Conservation--Events constraint absorbs third log_mu.

title: Getting Started with TemporalHazard
text: Picking right phase shape single biggest modeling decision multiphase fit. package ships canonical shapes SAS C HAZARD library: "cdf" — saturating curve \(\Phi(t) \[0, 1]\), parameterized t_half (time \(G(t_{1/2}) = 0.5\)), nu (time exponent), m (shape exponent). SAS “early” G1 shape. Use early phase, phase whose accumulated hazard saturates rather growing without bound. "constant" — \(\Phi(t) = t\). phase’s hazard rate flat; shape parameters estimate, scale \(\mu\). SAS G2 shape. Use background plateau. "g3" — SAS “late” shape, parameterized tau (time-scale), gamma (time exponent), alpha (shape parameter; \(\alpha = 0\) gives exponential limit), eta (outer exponent). Use late phase near-zero early accelerates time — graft deterioration years archetype. See ?hzr_phase additional "hazard" shape full parameterization . practice choose phase shapes looking Kaplan-Meier cumulative hazard plot, identifying regimes present, matching regime shape family whose behavior fits. fit, look decomposition plot, adjust starting values fix shapes phase doesn’t land expected. "g3" type uses four-parameter G3 decomposition original C/SAS HAZARD program, providing unbounded power-law growth late-phase hazards. See vignette("mf-mathematical-foundations") full mathematical treatment.
code: hzr_phase("cdf",      t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 1)   # Early risk (bounded) hzr_phase("constant")                                   # Flat background rate hzr_phase("cdf",      t_half = 10,  nu = 1, m = 0)    # Late risk (CDF-based) hzr_phase("g3",       tau = 1, gamma = 3, alpha = 1,   # Late risk (G3 power law)                        eta = 1)

text: package ships small set numerical helpers used internally keep likelihood evaluations stable across wide range arguments optimizer encounters. ’re exported can reach custom code debugging fit. common one hzr_log1pexp(x), computes \(\log(1 + e^x)\) numerically stable way. naive log(1 + exp(x)) overflows \(x\) exceeds 700 (exp(x) overflows); helper switches asymptotic \(x + \log(1 + e^{-x})\) large \(x\), exact floating-point precision. package uses inside every log-likelihood expression involves log-survival term, evaluation can run \(x = -50\) \(x = 5000\) without producing Inf NaN.

Fit univariable logistic regression candidate death indicator. p-values come final word whether covariate matters — ignore joint structure hazard model treat event time binary outcome — tell covariates chance mattering, deserve closer inspection. Figure 1: Exploratory: age vs. mortality LOESS smooth LOESS smooth reveals shape covariate-mortality relationship non-parametric way. roughly linear smooth means covariate enters hazard model natural scale; U inverted-U shape means polynomial non-monotone transform; plateau--rise means threshold effect may need binning. call make writing formula hazard(), staring converged--misspecified model. hzr_calibrate() bins continuous covariate quantile groups applies logit / Gompertz / Cox link transform, can eyeball whether covariate-outcome relationship linear chosen link scale. corresponds SAS logit.sas / logitgr.sas macros. roughly linear trend across groups means logit link appropriate; strong curvature flags need transform (example, polynomial log).
code: data(avc) avc <- na.omit(avc)  # Candidate covariates candidates <- c("age", "status", "mal", "com_iv", "inc_surg", "orifice") logit_fits <- lapply(candidates, function(var) {   fmla <- as.formula(paste("dead ~", var))   glm(fmla, data = avc, family = binomial()) }) names(logit_fits) <- candidates  # Which covariates are significant univariably? p_values <- vapply(logit_fits, function(f) {   coef(summary(f))[2, "Pr(>|z|)"] }, numeric(1))  data.frame(covariate = names(p_values),            p_value   = round(p_values, 4),            row.names = NULL) #>   covariate p_value #> 1       age  0.0017 #> 2    status  0.0000 #> 3       mal  0.0006 #> 4    com_iv  0.0000 #> 5  inc_surg  0.0114 #> 6   orifice  0.0034 ggplot(avc, aes(age, dead)) +   geom_jitter(height = 0.05, width = 0, alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +   geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE, colour = "#0072B2",               linewidth = 0.8) +   labs(x = "Age at operation (months)", y = "Death (0/1)") +   theme_minimal() #> `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x' age_cal <- hzr_calibrate(   x      = avc$age,   event  = avc$dead,   groups = 10,   link   = "logit" ) print(age_cal) #> Variable calibration (logit link, 10 groups) #>  #>  group  n events    mean     min     max  prob link_value #>      1 30     11   3.519   1.051   5.388 0.367     -0.547 #>      2 31     11   8.665   5.421  11.532 0.355     -0.598 #>      3 30     13  15.194  11.631  18.497 0.433     -0.268 #>      4 31     11  23.077  18.990  27.828 0.355     -0.598 #>      5 30      7  43.544  28.124  57.167 0.233     -1.190 #>      6 31      3  72.066  59.730  86.408 0.097     -2.234 #>      7 30      2 101.154  86.507 117.522 0.067     -2.639 #>      8 31      3 162.739 121.169 203.733 0.097     -2.234 #>      9 30      4 247.051 205.343 297.140 0.133     -1.872 #>     10 31      3 530.623 324.573 790.981 0.097     -2.234

title: Inference & Diagnostics
text: delta-method CIs predict(se.fit = TRUE) returns fast asymptotically correct, lean Hessian-derived parameter vcov — can mislead likelihood surface poorly behaved near MLE (boundary fits, near-degenerate parameter combinations, small samples). package flags cases : fit carries rcond pd diagnostics, summary() prints note (matching warning fit time) Hessian ill-conditioned positive-definite — strong signal prefer bootstrap. Bootstrap resampling robust alternative: refit model resampled dataset, collect resulting parameter prediction values, read empirical 2.5th / 97.5th percentiles 95% CI. ’s computationally heavier doesn’t assume likelihood locally quadratic, picks right tail behavior even delta-method theory creaks. hzr_bootstrap() wraps resample--refit loop corresponds SAS bootstrap.hazard.sas bootstrap.summary.sas macros. fit base model first; bootstrap replicates resample data refit using starting values. hzr_bootstrap() returns long data frame per-replicate coefficient estimates ($replicates) parameter-level summary (mean, SD, 95% percentile CI) $summary. use n_boot = 30 purely vignette renders reasonable time — real analysis ’d want 200 replicates. set.seed(42) call hzr_bootstrap() makes resample sequence reproducible. parameter-level CIs come directly bootstrap distribution. Prediction-level CIs (survival curve hazard profile) require pivoting boot$replicates wide format evaluating parametric survival formula per replicate. workflow scope section, building blocks returned object.
code: # Fit the base model that bootstrapping will use fit <- hazard(   Surv(int_dead, dead) ~ age + status + mal + com_iv,   data  = avc,   dist  = "weibull",   theta = c(mu = 0.20, nu = 1.0, rep(0, 4)),   fit   = TRUE,   control = list(maxit = 500) )  # Prediction grid at a median-risk profile t_grid <- seq(0.01, max(avc$int_dead) * 0.9, length.out = 100) base_nd <- data.frame(time = t_grid, age = median(avc$age),                       status = 2, mal = 0, com_iv = 0)  surv_point <- predict(fit, newdata = base_nd, type = "survival") set.seed(42) boot <- hzr_bootstrap(fit, n_boot = 30)  # kept small for vignette build time print(boot) #> Bootstrap inference for hazard model #> Mode: fixed refit  #> Replicates: 30 successful, 0 failed #>  #>  parameter  n pct    mean     sd     min    max ci_lower ci_upper #>         mu 30 100  0.0000 0.0000  0.0000 0.0000   0.0000   0.0000 #>         nu 30 100  0.2174 0.0603  0.0004 0.2668   0.0012   0.2587 #>        age 30 100 -0.0025 0.0024 -0.0100 0.0026  -0.0079   0.0011 #>     status 30 100  0.6778 0.1666  0.2712 1.0751   0.3792   0.9582 #>        mal 30 100  0.4165 0.3526 -0.4065 0.9703  -0.3595   0.9447 #>     com_iv 30 100  0.9099 0.4358  0.0609 2.0954   0.2661   2.0265

Figure 3: Sensitivity analysis: reference vs. high-risk profile gap curves quantifies clinical impact risk factors. sensitivity analysis informative combined bootstrap confidence intervals curve, showing whether difference statistically meaningful.
code: # Define reference and high-risk profiles ref_profile <- data.frame(   age    = median(avc$age),   status = 2,   mal    = 0,   com_iv = 0 )  high_risk <- data.frame(   age    = quantile(avc$age, 0.90),   status = 4,   mal    = 1,   com_iv = 1 ) sens_curves <- do.call(rbind, lapply(   list("Reference" = ref_profile, "High risk" = high_risk),   function(p) {     nd <- p[rep(1, length(t_grid)), ]     nd$time <- t_grid     data.frame(time = t_grid,                survival = predict(fit, newdata = nd, type = "survival") * 100,                Profile = deparse(substitute(p)))   } )) # Fix profile labels sens_curves$Profile <- rep(c("Reference", "High risk"),                            each = length(t_grid)) sens_curves$Profile <- factor(sens_curves$Profile,                               levels = c("Reference", "High risk"))  ggplot(sens_curves, aes(time, survival, colour = Profile)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c("Reference" = "#009E73",                                  "High risk" = "#D55E00")) +   scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +   labs(x = "Months after AVC repair", y = "Freedom from death (%)",        colour = NULL) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: Mathematical Foundations of TemporalHazard
text:

code: t_grid <- seq(0.01, 10, length.out = 200)  # Standard sigmoidal (Case 1: m > 0, nu > 0) d <- hzr_decompos(t_grid, t_half = 3, nu = 2, m = 1)  # Verify the half-life property: G(t_half) = 0.5 d_half <- hzr_decompos(3, t_half = 3, nu = 2, m = 1) cat("G(t_half) =", round(d_half$G, 6), "\n") #> G(t_half) = 0.5  # Verify the identity: h(t) = g(t) / (1 - G(t)) h_check <- d$g / (1 - d$G) cat("Max |h - g/(1-G)| =", max(abs(d$h - h_check)), "\n") #> Max |h - g/(1-G)| = 0 if (has_ggplot) {   library(ggplot2)    params <- list(     "Case 1: m=1, nu=2"     = list(nu = 2,   m = 1),     "Case 1L: m=0, nu=2"    = list(nu = 2,   m = 0),     "Case 2: m=-0.5, nu=2"  = list(nu = 2,   m = -0.5),     "Case 2L: m=-0.5, nu=0" = list(nu = 0,   m = -0.5),     "Case 3: m=1, nu=-0.5"  = list(nu = -0.5, m = 1),     "Case 3L: m=0, nu=-0.5" = list(nu = -0.5, m = 0)   )    t_grid <- seq(0.01, 10, length.out = 200)   rows <- list()    for (nm in names(params)) {     p <- params[[nm]]     d <- hzr_decompos(t_grid, t_half = 3, nu = p$nu, m = p$m)     rows <- c(rows, list(data.frame(       time = rep(t_grid, 3),       value = c(d$G, d$g, d$h),       quantity = rep(c("G(t) — CDF", "g(t) — density", "h(t) — hazard"),                      each = length(t_grid)),       case = nm     )))   }    df <- do.call(rbind, rows)    # Cap hazard display at reasonable values for readability   df$value[df$quantity == "h(t) — hazard" & df$value > 5] <- NA    ggplot(df, aes(x = time, y = value)) +     geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +     facet_grid(quantity ~ case, scales = "free_y") +     labs(x = "Time", y = NULL) +     theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +     theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 7)) }

title: Mathematical Foundations of TemporalHazard
text: total cumulative hazard decomposes additively across \(J\) phases: \[ H(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \mu_j(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \Phi_j(t;\, t_{1/2,j},\, \nu_j,\, m_j) \] : \(\mu_j(\mathbf{x}) = \exp(\alpha_j + \mathbf{x}_j \boldsymbol{\beta}_j)\) phase-specific log-linear scale covariates \(\Phi_j(t)\) temporal shape, determined phase type three phase types correspond different uses decomposition output: SAS/C bridge classic three-phase HAZARD model used: G1 (early) \(\\) hzr_phase("cdf", ...) G2 (constant) \(\\) hzr_phase("constant") G3 (late) \(\\) hzr_phase("hazard", ...) TemporalHazard generalizes \(N\) phases type. cumulative hazard, instantaneous hazard survival : \[ h(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \mu_j(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \varphi_j(t) \qquad\text{} \varphi_j = d\Phi_j/dt \] \[ S(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \exp\!\bigl(-H(t \mid \mathbf{x})\bigr) \] derivative \(\varphi_j(t)\) depends phase type: "cdf": \(\varphi(t) = g(t)\) (density) "hazard": \(\varphi(t) = h(t) = g(t)/(1 - G(t))\) "constant": \(\varphi(t) = 1\) math exposed R hzr_phase(), builds one phase time, hazard(), composes phases full model. #> <hzr_phase> cdf (early risk)  #>   t_half = 0.5  nu = 2  m = 0 print(const) #> <hzr_phase> constant (flat rate) print(late) #> <hzr_phase> hazard (late risk)  #>   t_half = 5  nu = 1  m = 0 if (has_ggplot) {   t_grid <- seq(0.01, 12, length.out = 200)    phi_early <- hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0,                                  type = "cdf")   phi_late  <- hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, t_half = 5, nu = 1, m = 0,                                  type = "hazard")   phi_const <- hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, type = "constant")    dphi_early <- hzr_phase_hazard(t_grid, t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0,                                   type = "cdf")   dphi_late  <- hzr_phase_hazard(t_grid, t_half = 5, nu = 1, m = 0,                                   type = "hazard")   dphi_const <- hzr_phase_hazard(t_grid, type = "constant")    df <- data.frame(     time = rep(t_grid, 6),     value = c(phi_early, phi_late, phi_const,               dphi_early, dphi_late, dphi_const),     phase = rep(rep(c("cdf (early)", "hazard (late)", "constant"),                     each = length(t_grid)), 2),     quantity = rep(c("Phi(t) — cumulative", "phi(t) — instantaneous"),                    each = 3 * length(t_grid))   )    ggplot(df, aes(x = time, y = value, colour = phase)) +     geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +     facet_wrap(~ quantity, scales =   mu_late  <- 0.2    H_early <- mu_early * hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, t_half = 0.5, nu = 2,                                            m = 0, type = "cdf")   H_const <- mu_const * hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, type = "constant")   H_late  <- mu_late  * hzr_phase_cumhaz(t_grid, t_half = 5, nu = 1,                                            m = 0, type = "hazard")   H_total <- H_early + H_const + H_late    df <- data.frame(     time = rep(t_grid, 4),     cumhaz = c(H_early, H_const, H_late, H_total),     component = rep(c("Early (cdf)", "Constant", "Late (hazard)", "Total"), component,                  linewidth = component)) +     geom_line() +     scale_colour_manual(values = c(       "Total" = "black", "Early (cdf)" = "#0072B2",       "Constant" = "#009E73", "Late Key features: Multi-start: optimizer runs \(k\) random perturbations around user-supplied starting values (default \(k = 5\), controlled control$n_starts). run highest log-likelihood kept. Feasibility guard: parameter vector \(m < 0\) \(\nu < 0\) phase returns \(-\infty\) immediately. Post-fit Hessian: numerical Hessian negative log-likelihood solution inverted produce variance-covariance matrix \(\hat{V}\), standard errors \(\sqrt{\text{diag}(\hat{V})}\). inversion hardened ill-conditioning arises high parameter counts: Hessian symmetrized, reciprocal condition number checked, inverted via Cholesky factorization, general solve() fallback Hessian positive-definite. Non-positive variance estimates flagged rather silently returned NaN standard errors. fit carries rcond (reciprocal condition number) pd (positive-definiteness) diagnostics; summary() prints note, warning raised, fit ill-conditioned positive-definite.

code: data(cabgkul)  fit_mp <- hazard(   Surv(int_dead, dead) ~ 1,   data   = cabgkul,   dist   = "multiphase",   phases = list(     early    = hzr_phase("cdf", t_half = 0.2, nu = 1, m = 1,                           fixed = "shapes"),     constant = hzr_phase("constant"),     late     = hzr_phase("g3",  tau = 1, gamma = 3, alpha = 1, eta = 1,                           fixed = "shapes")   ),   fit     = TRUE,   control = list(n_starts = 5, maxit = 1000) ) t_mp <- seq(0.01, max(cabgkul$int_dead) * 0.95, length.out = 200) nd   <- data.frame(time = t_mp)  decomp <- predict(fit_mp, newdata = nd, type = "cumulative_hazard",                   decompose = TRUE)  # Numerical differentiation: h(t) ≈ ΔH(t) / Δt num_hazard <- function(cumhaz, time) {   dt <- diff(time)   dH <- diff(cumhaz)   c(dH[1] / dt[1], dH / dt) }  h_long <- rbind(   data.frame(time = t_mp, hazard = num_hazard(decomp$early, t_mp),              Phase = "Early"),   data.frame(time = t_mp, hazard = num_hazard(decomp$constant, t_mp),              Phase = "Constant"),   data.frame(time = t_mp, hazard = num_hazard(decomp$late, t_mp),              Phase = "Late"),   data.frame(time = t_mp, hazard = num_hazard(decomp$total, t_mp),              Phase = "Total") ) h_long$Phase <- factor(h_long$Phase,                        levels = c("Total", "Early", "Constant", "Late"))  ggplot(h_long, aes(time, hazard, colour = Phase, linetype = Phase)) +   geom_line(aes(linewidth = Phase)) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c(Total = "#222222", Early = "#E69F00",                                  Constant = "#56B4E9", Late = "#CC79A7")) +   scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Total = "solid", Early = "dashed",                                    Constant = "dashed", Late = "dashed")) +   scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(Total = 1.3, Early = 0.7,                                     Constant = 0.7, Late = 0.7)) +   labs(x = "Months after CABG", y = "Hazard rate",        colour = "Phase", linetype = "Phase", linewidth = "Phase") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

text: SAS HAZARD analysis stack statements inside PROC HAZARD block. walk roughly order appear typical analysis script, showing SAS form corresponding R call. procedure-level statement names dataset sets global options. NOCOV / NOCOR flags suppress covariance correlation output; CONDITION= tolerance switch convergence check. Maps hazard() control list: Additional PROC HAZARD options direct R equivalent yet passed ... named arguments stored fit$legacy_args. Names follow-time variable. SAS HAZARD separate statement; R ’s first argument Surv() inside formula. Maps directly time: Must non-negative numeric vector time unit original analysis (months, AVC example). Missing values permitted. Names event-indicator variable. Like TIME, separate statement SAS HAZARD enters R formula Surv(). Maps status: TemporalHazard coerces status numeric; logical vectors also accepted. HAZARD convention uses 1 = occurred, 0 = censored/alive last contact. Supplies starting values optimizer flags parameters hold fixed (FIXM, FIXMU, etc.). starting values matter — multiphase optimizer particular, poor starting point can park fit local minimum well away global MLE. Maps theta (coefficient/parameter vector) control (fix flags): Note: Full SAS PARMS syntax mirrored one--one public API. current package, supply parameter vector directly via theta record fixed-parameter intent control$fix. legacy parity helpers generate SAS-style control text comparing historical binaries. statements assign covariates specific phases. SAS HAZARD block lists covariates affect phase starting coefficients. Covariates can appear multiple blocks different starting values — column, different phase-specific effect. HAZARD, EARLY CONSTANT define phase-specific covariate coefficients. TemporalHazard unified single design matrix x coefficient vector theta M1. Phase assignment formalised M2 multi-phase likelihood implemented. Current convention (M1): combine covariates x supply corresponding starting coefficients theta. Triggers stepwise covariate selection inside hazard fit. SLE significance level entry, SLS staying. SAS HAZARD embedded PROC HAZARD call; R stepwise loop separate hzr_stepwise() function wraps fitted hazard() object. TemporalHazard now ships hzr_stepwise(), implements forward, backward, two-way stepwise selection SAS-style SLENTRY / SLSTAY thresholds, phase-specific entry multiphase models, MOVE oscillation guard. FAST-screening (Lawless-Singhal approximate Wald updates) yet implemented; every candidate currently gets full refit. See ?hzr_stepwise full option list.
code: PROC HAZARD DATA=AVCS NOCOV NOCOR CONDITION=14; fit <- hazard(   ...,   control = list(     nocov      = TRUE,   # suppress covariance output     nocor      = TRUE,   # suppress correlation output     condition  = 14      # CONDITION= switch   ) ) TIME INT_DEAD; fit <- hazard(   time   = avcs$INT_DEAD,   ... ) EVENT DEAD; fit <- hazard(   status = avcs$DEAD,   # 1 = event, 0 = censored   ... ) PARMS MUE=0.3504743 THALF=0.1905077 NU=1.437416 M=1 FIXM       MUC=4.391673E-07; fit <- hazard(   theta   = c(MUE = 0.3504743, THALF = 0.1905077, NU = 1.437416,               M = 1,           MUC   = 4.391673e-07),   control = list(     fix = c("M")   # FIXM → freeze M during optimization   ),   ... ) EARLY  AGE=-0.03205774, COM_IV=1.336675, MAL=0.6872028,        OPMOS=-0.01963377, OP_AGE=0.0002086689, STATUS=0.5169533; CONSTANT INC_SURG=1.375285, ORIFICE=3.11765, STATUS=1.054988; # Build design matrix from the AVC data set X <- data.matrix(avcs[, c("AGE", "COM_IV", "MAL", "OPMOS", "OP_AGE",                            "STATUS", "INC_SURG", "ORIFICE")])  # Starting values from SAS EARLY + CONSTANT blocks combined theta_start <- c(   AGE      = -0.03205774,   COM_IV   =  1.336675,   MAL      =  0.6872028,   OPMOS    = -0.01963377,   OP_AGE   =  0.0002086689,   STATUS   =  0.5169533,   # EARLY phase coefficient   INC_SURG =  1.375285,   ORIFICE  =  3.11765 )  fit <- hazard(   time   = avcs$INT_DEAD,   status = avcs$DEAD,   x      = X,   theta  = theta_start,   dist   = "weibull" ) SELECTION SLE=0.2 SLS=0.1;

title: Migrating from SAS HAZARD to TemporalHazard
text: Supplies starting values optimizer flags parameters hold fixed (FIXM, FIXMU, etc.). starting values matter — multiphase optimizer particular, poor starting point can park fit local minimum well away global MLE. Maps theta (coefficient/parameter vector) control (fix flags): Note: Full SAS PARMS syntax mirrored one--one public API. current package, supply parameter vector directly via theta record fixed-parameter intent control$fix. legacy parity helpers generate SAS-style control text comparing historical binaries.
code: PARMS MUE=0.3504743 THALF=0.1905077 NU=1.437416 M=1 FIXM       MUC=4.391673E-07; fit <- hazard(   theta   = c(MUE = 0.3504743, THALF = 0.1905077, NU = 1.437416,               M = 1,           MUC   = 4.391673e-07),   control = list(     fix = c("M")   # FIXM → freeze M during optimization   ),   ... )

title: Migrating from SAS HAZARD to TemporalHazard
text: statements assign covariates specific phases. SAS HAZARD block lists covariates affect phase starting coefficients. Covariates can appear multiple blocks different starting values — column, different phase-specific effect. HAZARD, EARLY CONSTANT define phase-specific covariate coefficients. TemporalHazard unified single design matrix x coefficient vector theta M1. Phase assignment formalised M2 multi-phase likelihood implemented. Current convention (M1): combine covariates x supply corresponding starting coefficients theta.
code: EARLY  AGE=-0.03205774, COM_IV=1.336675, MAL=0.6872028,        OPMOS=-0.01963377, OP_AGE=0.0002086689, STATUS=0.5169533; CONSTANT INC_SURG=1.375285, ORIFICE=3.11765, STATUS=1.054988; # Build design matrix from the AVC data set X <- data.matrix(avcs[, c("AGE", "COM_IV", "MAL", "OPMOS", "OP_AGE",                            "STATUS", "INC_SURG", "ORIFICE")])  # Starting values from SAS EARLY + CONSTANT blocks combined theta_start <- c(   AGE      = -0.03205774,   COM_IV   =  1.336675,   MAL      =  0.6872028,   OPMOS    = -0.01963377,   OP_AGE   =  0.0002086689,   STATUS   =  0.5169533,   # EARLY phase coefficient   INC_SURG =  1.375285,   ORIFICE  =  3.11765 )  fit <- hazard(   time   = avcs$INT_DEAD,   status = avcs$DEAD,   x      = X,   theta  = theta_start,   dist   = "weibull" )

title: Migrating from SAS HAZARD to TemporalHazard
text: Triggers stepwise covariate selection inside hazard fit. SLE significance level entry, SLS staying. SAS HAZARD embedded PROC HAZARD call; R stepwise loop separate hzr_stepwise() function wraps fitted hazard() object. TemporalHazard now ships hzr_stepwise(), implements forward, backward, two-way stepwise selection SAS-style SLENTRY / SLSTAY thresholds, phase-specific entry multiphase models, MOVE oscillation guard. FAST-screening (Lawless-Singhal approximate Wald updates) yet implemented; every candidate currently gets full refit. See ?hzr_stepwise full option list.
code: SELECTION SLE=0.2 SLS=0.1;

title: Migrating from SAS HAZARD to TemporalHazard
text: Statement--statement mapping fine reference, full gestalt lands see complete SAS HAZARD analysis R translation side side. example final multivariable model examples/hm.death.AVC.sas reference C repository — death atrioventricular canal repair, two-phase model covariates assigned specific phases. ’s canonical “real SAS HAZARD analysis looks like” specimen. original SAS code, exactly appears reference distribution. Notice statements stack inside single %HAZARD() macro call. model TemporalHazard. Every SAS statement corresponding R argument : TIME EVENT collapse Surv(int_dead, dead) left formula; global covariate list goes right; PARMS starting values become theta vector; phase-specific assignments use formula argument inside hzr_phase(); FIXM becomes fixed = "shapes" (subset shape names). line--line correspondence point — ’ve translated one analysis way, pattern carries every .
code: %HAZARD( PROC HAZARD DATA=AVCS P CONSERVE OUTHAZ=OUTEST CONDITION=14 QUASI;      TIME INT_DEAD;      EVENT DEAD;      PARMS MUE=0.3504743 THALF=0.1905077 NU=1.437416 M=1 FIXM            MUC=4.391673E-07;      EARLY   AGE=-0.03205774, COM_IV=1.336675,  MAL=0.6872028,              OPMOS=-0.01963377, OP_AGE=0.0002086689, STATUS=0.5169533;      CONSTANT INC_SURG=1.375285, ORIFICE=3.11765, STATUS=1.054988; ); # Assumed: avcs is a data.frame read from the AVC flat file # (same variables as the SAS DATA step)  avcs <- avcs |>   transform(     LN_AGE   = log(AGE),     LN_OPMOS = log(OPMOS),     LN_INC   = ifelse(is.na(INC_SURG), NA, log(INC_SURG + 1)),     LN_NYHA  = log(STATUS)   )  # Replace missing INC_SURG with column mean (mirrors PROC STANDARD REPLACE) avcs$INC_SURG[is.na(avcs$INC_SURG)] <- mean(avcs$INC_SURG, na.rm = TRUE)  X <- data.matrix(avcs[, c("AGE", "COM_IV", "MAL", "OPMOS", "OP_AGE",                            "STATUS", "INC_SURG", "ORIFICE")])  fit <- hazard(   time    = avcs$INT_DEAD,   status  = avcs$DEAD,   x       = X,   theta   = c(     # Hazard shape parameters (from PARMS)     MUE   = 0.3504743,     THALF = 0.1905077,     NU    = 1.437416,     M     = 1,     MUC   = 4.391673e-07,     # Covariate coefficients (from EARLY + CONSTANT blocks)     AGE      = -0.03205774,     COM_IV   =  1.336675,     MAL      =  0.6872028,     OPMOS    = -0.01963377,     OP_AGE   =  0.0002086689,     STATUS   =  0.5169533,     INC_SURG =  1.375285,     ORIFICE  =  3.11765   ),   dist    = "weibull",   control = list(     condition = 14,     quasi     = TRUE,     conserve  = TRUE,     fix       = c("M")   # FIXM   ) )  fit

text: SAS HAZARD P (predict / print) option PROC HAZARD line writes predicted survival, hazard, cumulative-hazard tables output dataset. R predictions come predict.hazard() fitted object, requested quantity chosen via type= argument. predict.hazard() currently supports four output types — "linear_predictor", "hazard", "survival", "cumulative_hazard" — covering every quantity SAS P option produces: code chunk shows "linear_predictor" "hazard"; "survival" "cumulative_hazard" follow pattern. multiphase fits pass decompose = TRUE get per-phase cumulative hazard contributions instead just total.
code: # Linear predictor (X %*% theta) eta <- predict(fit, type = "linear_predictor")  # Hazard scale (exp(eta)) hz  <- predict(fit, type = "hazard")

title: Migrating from SAS HAZARD to TemporalHazard
text: SAS HAZARD veteran migrating TemporalHazard aware following scope limits v0.9.8. Detailed status per feature tracked inst/dev/SAS-PARITY-GAP-ANALYSIS.md inst/dev/DEVELOPMENT-PLAN.md. Supported: hzr_stepwise() implements forward / backward / two-way stepwise SAS-style SLENTRY / SLSTAY thresholds, per-phase entry multiphase, MOVE oscillation guard. yet supported: FAST-screening (Lawless-Singhal approximate Wald updates). Every candidate currently gets full refit, slower always correct. Supported: time_windows applies one piecewise-constant cut-point set across covariates. yet supported: distinct EARLY/LATE window sets per phase. Workaround: expand design matrix manually calling hazard(). R equivalents coef(fit) vcov(fit) memory; automatic dataset-export mode. saveRDS() need -disk artefact. predict.hazard() covers hazard, cumulative_hazard, survival, linear_predictor. Density quantile (median survival) types wired ; derive cumulative_hazard survival predictions needed. users migrating older TemporalHazard versions reading older SAS parity notes: weights distributions — shipped v0.9.6. Weibull, exponential, log-logistic, log-normal, multiphase honour observation weights end--end (LL + analytic gradient + multiphase Conservation Events). Surv(start, stop, event) start > 0 — shipped v0.9.7. Counting-process rows contribute H(stop) - H(start) Weibull multiphase. previous hazard() guard non-zero starts gone. Delta-method prediction confidence limits — shipped v0.9.8. Use predict(..., se.fit = TRUE, level = 0.95) get data frame fit, se.fit, lower, upper per row. Closed-form Jacobian Weibull multiphase, numDeriv::jacobian fallback exponential / log-logistic / log-normal.

code: library(TemporalHazard) data(cabgkul)  # Intercept-only Weibull on 5,880 CABG patients fit <- hazard(   survival::Surv(int_dead, dead) ~ 1,   data  = cabgkul,   dist  = "weibull",   theta = c(mu = 0.10, nu = 1.0),   fit   = TRUE ) summary(fit)

title: Temporal Parametric Hazard Modeling
text: phase specified hzr_phase(), sets temporal shape type starting values. optimizer estimates phase-specific scale parameters shape parameters jointly. Covariates supported via formula interface (see vignette("fitting-hazard-models")).
code: # Three-phase additive hazard decomposition fit_mp <- hazard(   survival::Surv(int_dead, dead) ~ 1,   data   = cabgkul,   dist   = "multiphase",   phases = list(     early    = hzr_phase("cdf", t_half = 0.2, nu = 1, m = 1,                           fixed = "shapes"),     constant = hzr_phase("constant"),     late     = hzr_phase("g3",  tau = 1, gamma = 3, alpha = 1, eta = 1,                           fixed = "shapes")   ),   fit = TRUE ) summary(fit_mp)  # Per-phase decomposition of cumulative hazard t_grid <- seq(0.01, max(cabgkul$int_dead) * 0.9, length.out = 200) predict(fit_mp, newdata = data.frame(time = t_grid),         type = "cumulative_hazard", decompose = TRUE)

what: TemporalHazard: Temporal Parametric Hazard Modeling — TemporalHazard-package
title: TemporalHazard: Temporal Parametric Hazard Modeling — TemporalHazard-package
text: Native R implementation multiphase parametric hazard model Blackstone, Naftel, Turner (1986), focus behavioral parity, transparent numerics, reproducible validation original ‘C’/‘SAS’ HAZARD program.  package fits time-varying hazards additive sum parametric phases — early, constant, late risk streams — carrying covariate effects.

title: TemporalHazard: Temporal Parametric Hazard Modeling — TemporalHazard-package
text: total cumulative hazard decomposes additively across \(J\) phases: $$H(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \mu_j(\mathbf{x}) \,       \Phi_j(t)$$ \(\mu_j(\mathbf{x}) = \exp(\alpha_j + \mathbf{x}_j^\top \beta_j)\) phase-specific log-linear scale (intercept plus covariate effects) \(\Phi_j(t)\) temporal shape contributed phase \(j\), parameters depending phase type (see phase vocabulary ).  instantaneous hazard survival follow directly: $$h(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \mu_j(\mathbf{x}) \,       \varphi_j(t), \qquad       S(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \exp\!\bigl(-H(t \mid \mathbf{x})\bigr)$$ \(\varphi_j = d\Phi_j/dt\).  phase specified hzr_phase() model fit maximum likelihood hazard().

title: TemporalHazard: Temporal Parametric Hazard Modeling — TemporalHazard-package
text: \(G(t)\) generalized temporal decomposition CDF computed hzr_decompos(), \(G_3(t)\) unbounded late-phase intensity hzr_decompos_g3().  See vignette("mf-mathematical-foundations") full derivation.

title: TemporalHazard: Temporal Parametric Hazard Modeling — TemporalHazard-package
text: classic three-phase HAZARD model maps directly onto hzr_phase() calls: TemporalHazard generalizes fixed three-phase structure \(N\) phases type.  hzr_argument_mapping() gives full parameter translation table SAS/C parameterization R arguments.

title: TemporalHazard: Temporal Parametric Hazard Modeling — TemporalHazard-package
text: Model fitting hazard() — build fit single- multiphase models; hzr_phase() — specify one phase; hzr_stepwise() — forward, backward, bidirectional covariate selection. Prediction predict() fitted hazard object — survival, cumulative hazard, per-phase decomposed hazard; summary() — coefficient tables Wald inference. Parametric family hzr_decompos() — early-phase (G1) decomposition \(G(t)\), \(g(t)\), \(h(t)\); hzr_decompos_g3() — late-phase (G3) intensity; hzr_phase_cumhaz() hzr_phase_hazard() — per-phase \(\Phi(t)\) \(\varphi(t)\). Diagnostics hzr_kaplan(), hzr_nelson() — nonparametric references; hzr_gof() — goodness fit; hzr_calibrate(), hzr_deciles() — calibration; hzr_bootstrap() — resampling CIs; hzr_competing_risks() — cumulative incidence.

code: data(cabgkul)  # Kaplan-Meier survival km <- survival::survfit(survival::Surv(int_dead, dead) ~ 1, data = cabgkul) plot(km, xlab = "Months after CABG", ylab = "Survival",      main = "CABGKUL: Kaplan-Meier survival (n = 5,880)")   # \donttest{ # Single-phase Weibull fit with parametric overlay fit <- hazard(survival::Surv(int_dead, dead) ~ 1, data = cabgkul,               dist = "weibull", theta = c(mu = 0.10, nu = 1.0), fit = TRUE) t_grid <- seq(0.01, max(cabgkul$int_dead) * 0.9, length.out = 200) surv   <- predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(time = t_grid),                   type = "survival") plot(km, xlab = "Months after CABG", ylab = "Survival",      main = "CABGKUL: Weibull vs. Kaplan-Meier") lines(t_grid, surv, col = "blue", lwd = 2) legend("bottomleft", c("KM", "Weibull"), col = c("black", "blue"),        lty = 1, lwd = c(1, 2))  # }

Used status %% c(-1, 2); defaults time NULL. x Optional design matrix (data frame coercible matrix). time_windows Optional numeric vector strictly positive cut points piecewise time-varying coefficients. provided, predictor column x expanded one column per time window window gets coefficient. theta Optional numeric coefficient vector (starting values optimization). dist Character baseline distribution label (default "weibull"). One "weibull", "exponential", "loglogistic", "lognormal", "multiphase".  single-distribution families differ shape hazard traces time; "multiphase" builds additive N-phase hazard requires phases.  See Baseline distributions section means use . phases Optional named list hzr_phase() objects specifying phases multiphase model (dist = "multiphase").  See Examples. fit Logical; TRUE, fit model via maximum likelihood (default FALSE). weights Optional numeric vector observation weights (non-negative). observation's log-likelihood contribution multiplied weight. title: Build and optionally fit a hazard model — hazard
text: dist = "multiphase" cumulative hazard, instantaneous hazard, survival $$H(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \mu_j(\mathbf{x}) \, \Phi_j(t),       \qquad       h(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \mu_j(\mathbf{x}) \, \varphi_j(t),       \qquad       S(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \exp\!\bigl(-H(t \mid \mathbf{x})\bigr)$$ \(\mu_j(\mathbf{x}) = \exp(\alpha_j + \mathbf{x}_j^\top \beta_j)\) temporal shapes \(\Phi_j\), \(\varphi_j\) set phase's type (see hzr_phase()).  proportional-hazards single-phase families ("weibull", "exponential") special case \(J = 1\), covariates acting multiplicatively one temporal shape.  "loglogistic" (proportional-odds) "lognormal" (accelerated-failure-time) families place covariates differently — odds failure log-time location, respectively — separate parameterizations, special cases additive form.  Parameters estimated unconstrained internal scale (e.g. \(\log\mu\), \(\log t_{1/2}\)) transformed back reporting; see vignette("mf-mathematical-foundations").

title: Build and optionally fit a hazard model — hazard
text:
dist argument selects parametric form baseline hazard.  four single-distribution families differ shape hazard traces follow-; choose risk expected time.  "multiphase" general additive model lets several shapes coexist. "weibull" — monotone rising falling hazard (default) workhorse parametric model: \(H(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = (\mu t)^
u     \exp(\eta)\), hazard \(h \propto t^{
u - 1}\).  single shape \(
u\) makes risk increase time (\(
u > 1\)), decrease (\(
u < 1\)), stay flat (\(
u = 1\)).  Use default single monotone trend describes hazard. "exponential" — constant hazard memoryless special case \(
u = 1\): time-invariant baseline rate, \(H(t \mid \mathbf{x}) =     \mu t \exp(\eta)\).  Use event rate change follow-time (constant background risk also appears "constant" phase multiphase model). "loglogistic" — unimodal (rise--fall) hazard log-logistic proportional-odds form (covariates act multiplicatively odds failure, \(\exp(\eta)\), AFT time shift) whose hazard rises single peak declines shape exceeds 1 (monotone decreasing otherwise), heavier tails log-normal.  Use risk climbs early peak eases . "lognormal" — early-peaking, resolving hazard accelerated-failure-time form \(\log\) time Gaussian; hazard rises early peak decays toward zero.  Use risk concentrated early resolves time. "multiphase" — additive N-phase hazard Sums several phase shapes one model, \(H = \sum_j \mu_j(\mathbf{x}) \Phi_j(t)\), overall hazard can fall, level , rise within one fit. Requires phases; see hzr_phase() available phase shapes.  form reproduces classic C/SAS HAZARD models.

title: Bootstrap resampling for hazard model coefficients — hzr_bootstrap
text: Resample data replacement, refit hazard model replicate, accumulate coefficient distributions. Returns tidy data frame per-replicate estimates summary statistics. R equivalent SAS bootstrap.hazard.sas macro.

title: Bootstrap resampling for hazard model coefficients — hzr_bootstrap
code: hzr_bootstrap(   object,   n_boot = 200L,   fraction = 1,   seed = NULL,   verbose = FALSE,   scope = NULL,   direction = c("both", "forward", "backward"),   criterion = c("wald", "aic"),   slentry = 0.3,   slstay = 0.2,   max_steps = 50L,   max_move = 4L,   force_in = character(),   force_out = character(),   ... )  # S3 method for class 'hzr_bootstrap' print(x, digits = 4, ...)

title: Bootstrap resampling for hazard model coefficients — hzr_bootstrap
text: object fitted hazard object (fit = TRUE). n_boot Integer: number bootstrap replicates (default 200). fraction Numeric (0, 1]: fraction data sample per replicate (default 1.0 full bootstrap; < 1 bagging). seed Optional integer random seed reproducibility. supplied, set.seed(seed) called function entry, jumping global RNG seeded state; restored exit. Pass NULL (default) skip set.seed() call start caller's current RNG state. Note bootstrap consumes random numbers either way, global RNG state advance call – seed = NULL avoids reset entry, advance resampling. verbose Logical; TRUE, print progress every 50 replicates. scope Candidate variable scope embedded stepwise selection bootstrap replicate. NULL (default) preserves original fixed-formula bootstrap: every replicate refits object's exact model, summary$pct always ~100. supplied (one-sided formula, character vector, – multiphase fits – named list one-sided formulas keyed phase, matching hzr_stepwise()'s scope), replicate runs fresh hzr_stepwise() selection instead; see Details. direction, criterion, slentry, slstay, max_steps, max_move, force_in, force_out Passed hzr_stepwise() replicate scope supplied; ignored scope = NULL. See hzr_stepwise() definitions defaults. ... Additional arguments forwarded hzr_stepwise() (e.g. control = list(n_starts = 1)) scope supplied; ignored otherwise. x hzr_bootstrap object. digits Number decimal places formatting.

title: Bootstrap resampling for hazard model coefficients — hzr_bootstrap
text: list class "hzr_bootstrap" containing: replicates Data frame columns replicate, parameter, estimate – one row per parameter per successful replicate. summary Data frame columns parameter, n, pct, mean, sd, min, max, ci_lower, ci_upper – one row per parameter. mode = "select", pct selection frequency statistics conditional selection. n_success Number successfully converged replicates. n_failed Number replicates failed converge. mode "refit" (fixed-formula bootstrap) "select" (embedded stepwise selection). scope present mode == "select": candidate scope used.

title: Bootstrap resampling for hazard model coefficients — hzr_bootstrap
text: scope supplied, replicate instead runs fresh hzr_stepwise() selection resampled data (starting fixed-shape refit object) instead refitting object's exact formula. R equivalent SAS %HAZBOOT macro: fit hazard shape covariates (fixing via hzr_phase(..., fixed = "shapes")), bootstrap-screen candidate covariates often enter model. summary$pct reports selection frequency across replicates, summary$mean/sd/ci_* describe coefficient distribution conditional selection.

what: Calibrate a continuous variable against an outcome — hzr_calibrate
title: Calibrate a continuous variable against an outcome — hzr_calibrate
text: Group continuous covariate quantile bins, compute event probability (hazard rate) per bin, apply link transform (logit, Gompertz, Cox). R equivalent SAS logit.sas logitgr.sas macros.

title: Calibrate a continuous variable against an outcome — hzr_calibrate
code: hzr_calibrate(   x,   event,   groups = 10L,   by = NULL,   link = c("logit", "gompertz", "cox"),   time = NULL )

title: Calibrate a continuous variable against an outcome — hzr_calibrate
text: x Numeric vector: continuous covariate calibrate. event Numeric vector: event indicator (1 = event, 0 = event). groups Integer: number quantile bins (default 10). Optional factor character vector stratified calibration (SAS logitgr.sas functionality). provided, calibration computed within stratum. Default NULL (stratification). link Character: transform apply event probabilities. One "logit" (default), "gompertz" (complementary log-log), "cox". time Optional numeric vector: follow-time, required link = "cox". Cox link computes \(\log(\text{events} / \sum \text{time})\) (constant hazard rate).

title: Calibrate a continuous variable against an outcome — hzr_calibrate
text: data frame one row per group (per group--stratum combination) columns: group Integer group label. Stratum level (present provided). n Number observations group. events Number events. mean Mean x within group. min Minimum x within group. max Maximum x within group. prob Event probability (events / n), Cox link: events / sum(time). link_value Transformed probability chosen link scale.

title: Calibrate a continuous variable against an outcome — hzr_calibrate
text: Use function model entry assess whether covariate relationship outcome approximately linear link scale. transformed probabilities roughly linear group means, covariate can enter model untransformed. Curvature suggests transformation (log, quadratic) may improve fit.

title: Late-phase (G3) temporal decomposition — hzr_decompos_g3
text: Computes cumulative intensity \(G_3(t)\) derivative \(g_3(t) = dG_3/dt\) late-phase parametric family used original Blackstone C/SAS HAZARD code.  Unlike hzr_decompos() (computes early-phase G1 – bounded CDF), function can produce unbounded values, making suitable modelling increasing late risk.

title: Late-phase (G3) temporal decomposition — hzr_decompos_g3
text: \(\alpha > 0\): $$G_3(t) = \bigl(\bigl((t/\tau)^\gamma + 1\bigr)^{1/\alpha}                       - 1\bigr)^\eta$$ \(\alpha = 0\) (limiting exponential case): $$G_3(t) = \bigl(\exp\bigl((t/\tau)^\gamma\bigr) - 1\bigr)^\eta$$

text: time Numeric vector follow-times. status Numeric event indicator (1 = event, 0 = censored). conf_level Confidence level interval (default 0.95). SAS default 0.68268948 corresponds 1-SD interval. event_only Logical; TRUE (default), return rows event times (n_event > 0). FALSE, return rows times reported survival::survfit() (events censoring times).

title: Kaplan-Meier survival with exact logit confidence limits — hzr_kaplan
text: data frame one row per time point columns: time Event/censoring time. n_risk Number risk start interval. n_event Number events time. n_censor Number censored time. survival Kaplan-Meier survival estimate. std_err Standard error survival (Greenwood). cl_lower Lower confidence limit (logit-transformed). cl_upper Upper confidence limit (logit-transformed). cumhaz Cumulative hazard \(= -\log(S)\). hazard Interval hazard rate \(= \log(S_{t-1} / S_t) / \Delta t\). density Probability density estimate \(= (S_{t-1} - S_t) / \Delta t\). life Restricted mean survival time (area curve time).

title: Kaplan-Meier survival with exact logit confidence limits — hzr_kaplan
text: standard Greenwood confidence interval can exceed \([0, 1]\) tails. logit-transformed interval avoids working log-odds scale: $$   \text{CL}_{\text{lower}} = S / \bigl(S + (1-S)\,   \exp(z_\alpha\,\text{SI})\bigr) $$ $$   \text{CL}_{\text{upper}} = S / \bigl(S + (1-S)\,   \exp(-z_\alpha\,\text{SI})\bigr) $$ \(\text{SI} = \sqrt{V_P - 1} / (1 - S)\), \(V_P\) cumulative Greenwood variance product, \(z_\alpha\) normal quantile requested confidence level.

title: Kaplan-Meier survival with exact logit confidence limits — hzr_kaplan
text: Kaplan EL, Meier P (1958). Nonparametric estimation incomplete observations. J Stat Assoc 53(282):457–481. doi:10.1080/01621459.1958.10501452 Greenwood M (1926). natural duration cancer. Reports Public Health Medical Subjects 33:1–26.

what: Numerically stable log(1 - exp(-x)) for x > 0 — hzr_log1mexp
title: Numerically stable log(1 - exp(-x)) for x > 0 — hzr_log1mexp
text: Computes $$\mathrm{log1mexp}(x) = \log\!\bigl(1 - e^{-x}\bigr), \qquad x > 0$$ accurately across full range.  Following Mächler (2012), evaluation switches \(x = \log 2\): small \(x\) uses \(\log(-\mathrm{expm1}(-x))\) (avoiding cancellation \(x \0\)), larger \(x\) uses \(\mathrm{log1p}(-e^{-x})\) (avoiding loss precision \(x \\infty\)).  Non-positive non-finite inputs return NA.

Numerically stable log(1 + exp(x)) — hzr_log1pexp
text: Computes "softplus" function $$\mathrm{log1pexp}(x) = \log\!\bigl(1 + e^{x}\bigr)$$ without overflow.  naive log(1 + exp(x)) overflows Inf \(x \gtrsim 710\) even though true value \(\approx x\).  identity \(\log(1 + e^{x}) = x + \log(1 + e^{-x})\) \(x > 0\) keeps every intermediate finite.

title: Specify a single hazard phase — hzr_phase
text: type Character; phase's temporal shape — one "cdf" (early resolving risk), "hazard" (accumulating G1 aging risk), "g3" (late rising risk, original C/SAS late phase), "constant" (flat background rate).  See Phase types section means use . t_half Positive scalar; initial half-life (time \(G(t_{1/2}) = 0.5\)).  Used "cdf" "hazard" phases. SAS early: THALF/RHO. nu Numeric scalar; initial time exponent.  Used "cdf" "hazard" phases.  SAS early: NU. m Numeric scalar; initial shape exponent.  Used "cdf" "hazard" phases.  SAS early: M. tau Positive scalar; scale parameter "g3" phases. SAS late: TAU. gamma Positive scalar; time exponent "g3" phases. SAS late: GAMMA. alpha Non-negative scalar; shape parameter "g3" phases. alpha > 0, generic G3 formula used; alpha = 0 gives exponential limiting case.  SAS late: ALPHA. eta Positive scalar; outer exponent "g3" phases. SAS late: ETA. formula Optional one-sided formula (e.g. ~ age + nyha) phase-specific covariates.  NULL (default), phase inherits global formula hazard(). fixed Character vector naming shape parameters hold fixed optimization.  Valid names "cdf"/"hazard": "t_half", "nu", "m", "shapes" (shorthand three).  Valid names "g3": "tau", "gamma", "alpha", "eta", "shapes" (shorthand four).  Fixed parameters held starting values; mu (covariates) estimated.  Ignored "constant" phases. mirrors SAS/C HAZARD workflow shapes typically fixed scale parameters estimated. x hzr_phase object (print.hzr_phase()). ... Additional arguments (ignored).

title: Specify a single hazard phase — hzr_phase
text: S3 object class "hzr_phase" elements: type Phase type string. t_half Initial half-life (cdf/hazard phases). nu Initial time exponent (cdf/hazard phases). m Initial shape exponent (cdf/hazard phases). tau Scale parameter (g3 phases). gamma Time exponent (g3 phases). alpha Shape parameter (g3 phases). eta Outer exponent (g3 phases). formula Phase-specific formula NULL. fixed Character vector fixed parameter names (may empty).

title: Specify a single hazard phase — hzr_phase
text: phase one term \(j\) additive cumulative hazard $$H(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \sum_{j=1}^{J} \mu_j(\mathbf{x}) \,       \Phi_j(t)$$ \(\mu_j(\mathbf{x}) = \exp(\alpha_j + \mathbf{x}_j^\top \beta_j)\) phase-specific log-linear scale \(\Phi_j(t)\) temporal shape selected type ().  t_half/nu/m (g3 tau/gamma/alpha/eta) arguments set starting values shape; formula attaches covariates \(\mathbf{x}_j\) enter \(\mu_j\).

title: Specify a single hazard phase — hzr_phase
text: type argument chooses temporal shape \(\Phi_j(t)\) phase. captures qualitatively different pattern risk time; typical clinical model combines early, constant, late phase total hazard can fall, level , rise . "cdf" — early, resolving risk Named cumulative distribution function: phase contributes \(\Phi(t) = G(t)\), bounded CDF temporal decomposition (\(0\) \(t = 0\), rising ceiling \(1\)).  saturates, hazard adds, \(\mu\,g(t)\), peaks early decays toward zero — signature one-time insult patients either succumb survive past, e.g. peri-operative mortality.  Shape set t_half, nu, m. SAS/C equivalent: Early (G1) phase. "hazard" — accumulating aging risk (G1 family) Named phase contributes cumulative hazard built G1 family: \(\Phi(t) = -\log(1 - G(t))\), unbounded monotone increasing.  hazard \(\mu\,h(t)\) rises without leveling , models risk grows subjects age.  alternative late-risk form derived G1; original SAS/C late phase prefer "g3". Shape set t_half, nu, m. "g3" — late, rising risk (original C/SAS late phase) Named G3 (third) decomposition family used original HAZARD program late phase.  contributes \(\Phi(t) = G_3(t)\) hzr_decompos_g3(), unbounded intensity four-parameter shape (tau, gamma, alpha, eta) flexible G1-derived "hazard" form capturing accelerating late mortality (e.g. structural valve deterioration years surgery).  Use reproducing classic three-phase HAZARD models.  SAS/C equivalent: Late (G3) phase. "constant" — flat background rate time-invariant hazard: \(\Phi(t) = t\), added hazard \(\mu\) constant (exponential model).  represents steady, ongoing risk present follow-times, independent long ago time origin .  Takes shape parameters — scale \(\mu\) (covariates) estimated.  SAS/C equivalent: Constant (G2) phase. shape derivative \(\varphi_j = d\Phi_j/dt\) (forms instantaneous hazard contribution \(\mu_j\,\varphi_j(t)\)) \(g(t)\) "cdf", \(h(t)\) "hazard", \(g_3(t)\) "g3", \(1\) "constant".

title: Specify a single hazard phase — hzr_phase
code: # Classic 3-phase Blackstone pattern early <- hzr_phase("cdf",      t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0) const <- hzr_phase("constant") late  <- hzr_phase("g3", tau = 1, gamma = 3, alpha = 1, eta = 1)  # Fix all shapes (C/SAS-style: only estimate mu) early_fixed <- hzr_phase("cdf", t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0,                           fixed = "shapes") late_fixed  <- hzr_phase("g3", tau = 1, gamma = 3, alpha = 1, eta = 1,                           fixed = "shapes")  # Fix only some parameters early_partial <- hzr_phase("cdf", t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0,                             fixed = c("nu", "m"))  # Phase with specific covariates early_cov <- hzr_phase("cdf", t_half = 0.5, nu = 2, m = 0,                         formula = ~ age + shock)  # Use in hazard(): # hazard(Surv(time, status) ~ age, data = dat, #        dist = "multiphase", #        phases = list(early = early, constant = const, late = late))

text: time Numeric vector times (> 0). t_half Half-life parameter (> 0). nu Time exponent. m Shape parameter. type Phase type: "cdf" (early – uses \(G(t)\)), "hazard" (late – uses cumulative hazard \(h(t)\)), "constant" (flat rate – \(\Phi = t\)).

title: Cumulative hazard contribution from a single phase — hzr_phase_cumhaz
text: "cdf": \(\Phi(t) = G(t)\).  Bounded \([0, 1]\).  Models early risk resolves time. "hazard": \(\Phi(t) = -\log(1 - G(t))\).  Monotone increasing. Models late aging risk.  cumulative hazard derived hazard function \(h(t)\), since \(\int_0^t h(s)\,ds = -\log(1 - G(t))\). "constant": \(\Phi(t) = t\).  Ignores t_half, nu, m. Equivalent exponential (constant hazard rate).

title: Stepwise covariate selection for a parametric hazard model — hzr_stepwise
text: fit fitted hazard object built via formula = Surv(...) ~ predictors, data = df interface. scope Candidate set.  NULL (default) uses every data-frame column already model every phase.  single-distribution fits, pass one-sided formula (~ age + nyha) character vector names.  multiphase fits, pass named list one-sided formulas keyed phase. data Data frame base fit built .  Required refits. direction Search strategy — one "" (default), "forward", "backward".  Controls whether variables may enter, leave, .  See Selection direction criterion section. criterion Entry / retention rule — one "wald" (default) "aic".  "wald" applies SAS-style p-value thresholds (slentry / slstay); "aic" adds drops whenever lowers AIC.  See Selection direction criterion section. slentry Entry p-value threshold Wald criterion. Default 0.30 matches SAS SLENTRY. slstay Retention p-value threshold Wald criterion. Default 0.20 matches SAS SLSTAY. max_steps Hard cap total accepted actions.  Emits warning() hit.  Default 50. max_move Per-variable oscillation cap.  variable entered + exited max_move times frozen remainder run.  Default 4. force_in Character vector variables must remain model.  variables still scored reported selection trace, never dropped. force_out Character vector variables may never considered candidates. trace Logical; print step--step progress console. Default TRUE. ... Unused. x hzr_stepwise object. object hzr_stepwise object.
